title: Collection of Mouse Cerebrospinal Fluid from the Cisterna Magna
author: Aisha Sati

steps.title: Expose cisterna magna
steps.instruction: Separate the subcutaneous tissue and the muscles (m. biventer cervicis and m. rectus capitis dorsalis major) by blunt dissection with forceps; gently separate the muscles until the dura becomes visible, taking care not to pinch or destroy the dura, and retract the overlaying muscles to either side to expose the cisterna magna.

steps.title: Prepare pulled glass capillary
steps.instruction: Use a micropipette puller to pull glass capillaries suitable for piercing the cisterna magna and collecting CSF.

steps.title: Mount and break capillary tip
steps.instruction: Mount the sharpened capillary on a micromanipulator, connect its opposite end to thin tubing that is attached to a syringe for CSF collection; then break the tip by grasping it with straight forceps at approximately a 40° angle about halfway along the pulled tip, leaving a tip diameter of roughly 10–20 µm.

steps.title: Load syringe and attach to arm
steps.instruction: Push out air from the syringe, then fix the syringe‑capillary assembly on the descending arm of the stereotaxic apparatus.

steps.title: Anesthetize mouse
steps.instruction: Inject intraperitoneally a cocktail of 0.15 ml Nimatek, 0.2 ml Domitor and 1.5 ml sterile saline (dose 0.1 ml per 10 g body weight); verify depth of anesthesia by checking the toe‑pinch response.

steps.title: Secure mouse in apparatus
steps.instruction: Place the fully anesthetized animal on a heating pad and secure the head in the stereotaxic apparatus using ear bars.

steps.title: Incise skin and clean field
steps.instruction: Cut away fur on the dorsal neck region, make a sagittal skin incision, then make small lateral incisions to the left and right to expose the underlying muscle; clean the surgical field of blood and hair with small amounts of saline solution applied to cotton buds.

steps.title: Insert capillary into cisterna magna
steps.instruction: Using the prepared capillary, pierce the dura of the cisterna magna so that the tip lies within the cavity without touching tissue or blood vessels; puncture in the middle of the triangular area away from major blood vessels (site may vary slightly between mice).

steps.title: Collect CSF with negative pressure
steps.instruction: Carefully apply a slight negative pressure by pulling the syringe plunger while observing the capillary through the microscope; if more CSF is needed, allow the cisterna to refill and, when pressure returns to a normal level (often indicated by vessel pulsation), slowly apply additional negative pressure.

steps.title: Remove capillary after collection
steps.instruction: Wait until the pressure in the cisterna returns to a normal level again, then gently withdraw the capillary from the cavity.

steps.title: Transfer CSF to low‑binding tube
steps.instruction: Collect the harvested CSF from the capillary into a protein low‑binding Eppendorf tube.

steps.title: Centrifuge CSF and collect supernatant
steps.instruction: Spin the CSF at 10 000 × g, 4 °C for 10 minutes; then pipet the supernatant into a new protein low‑binding Eppendorf tube.

steps.title: Store samples at –80 °C
steps.instruction: Store the processed CSF samples at –80 °C until further use.

steps.title: Troubleshoot visibility or collection issues
steps.instruction: If the triangular landmark is not well visible or CSF is not entering the glass capillary, adjust the angle of the mouse’s head.
